channel.title: The Signal
channel.description: A daily briefing on developments that changed the picture today, with maps, full reports and sources.

item.title: Tuesday 20 October 2026
item.description:
Albertans voted by about three to one to stay in Canada, turning down a path toward a separation referendum. Oil climbed toward $112 as Iran claimed mine strikes on tankers in Hormuz and Saudi Arabia shot down a Houthi missile aimed at Riyadh. President Trump said it was time for someone else to negotiate for Ukraine, hours after a Russian drone killed six people in a park. France had its first calm night under curfews, a man was charged over the attack on Australian MP Helen Haines, and Super Typhoon Champi is now forecast to turn away from Taiwan. In Frontiers: a hacker who used AI agents to break into more than 100 company websites, and an FDA approval that can spare some cancer patients surgery.

  • Albertans reject a path to separation by about three to one
  • Oil climbs toward $112 as Iran claims tanker mine strikes and Houthis aim at Riyadh
  • Trump says someone else should negotiate for Ukraine as a drone kills six in a park
  • Man charged over attack on MP Helen Haines, who has lost a leg
  • France has a calm night under its first curfews as Macron tours the Gulf
  • Trump's approval falls to 31% as early voting opens in record numbers
  • A week before Israel votes, Hegseth visits and the polls stay tied
  • Super Typhoon Champi is now forecast to turn away from Taiwan and Luzon
  • Israeli police arrest 10 after settlers attack diplomats and a journalist

item.title: Monday 19 October 2026
item.description:
Russia answered Ukraine's weekend drone raid with an overnight strike on the grid that cut power to 550,000 homes, while US sanctions on Moscow stay paused. In Yemen, a Houthi missile strike on an army camp killed at least 53 recruits, officials said by evening, and Saudi Arabia put off its flagship investment conference to 2027. France's prime minister asked towns to impose curfews, and cost-of-living clashes spread to Milan. Albertans finish voting today on whether to start down the road out of Canada, and Israel's election, eight days off, is deadlocked. This afternoon Japan launched MMX, a mission to bring back the first soil from a moon of Mars.

  • Russia strikes back at Ukraine's grid, cutting power to 550,000 homes
  • Houthi missiles kill at least 18 soldiers at a Yemeni army camp
  • France turns to curfews as cost-of-living clashes reach Milan
  • Israel's election is deadlocked, and Trump endorses Netanyahu
  • Alberta votes on separation after 1.3 million ballots cast early
  • Congo's Ebola outbreak reaches an eighth province
  • Super Typhoon Champi heads for the Philippines and Taiwan after skirting Guam
  • Brazil's runoff tightens after a chaotic first debate
  • Australian MP critically hurt in what Albanese calls a deliberate attack

item.title: Sunday 18 October 2026
item.description:
France counted the cost of its worst unrest in years, and Macron answered with a promise of accountability and local protest bans. Ukraine sent more than a thousand drones into Russia hours after Washington waived the sanctions meant to squeeze Moscow's oil money. Brent crude sits near $110 as the Saudi–Houthi war widens, and Ebola is spreading person to person in Kenya for the first time. Two votes are close: Alberta decides tomorrow whether to start down the road out of Canada, and Brazil picks a president next Sunday.

  • France counts the damage, and waits for Macron
  • Ukraine sends 1,000 drones into Russia as Washington waives sanctions
  • Oil nears $110 as the Saudi–Houthi war widens
  • Ebola is now spreading inside Kenya
  • Alberta votes tomorrow on starting the road out of Canada
  • Trump's approval hits a record low with 16 days to go
  • Brazil's runoff is a coin toss, one week out
  • Settlers attack European diplomats as Washington tells Israel to crack down
  • Pakistan and the Taliban keep trading fire on the border
